title: The Inspector Window
description: Understand components, adding/removing them, debug mode, and presets.

slides.title: Inspector Basics 🛠️
slides.content:
# The Inspector Window

When you select a GameObject, the Inspector shows all its **components**. Every object has at least a **Transform** component (position, rotation, scale).

- Components are the building blocks of behavior: Mesh Renderer, Collider, Scripts, etc.
- You can **drag to reorder** components (important for script execution order).
- Right‑click a component to **Remove**, **Copy**, **Paste**, or **Reset** it.

quizData.question: What component does every GameObject have by default?
quizData.explanation: Every GameObject has a Transform component to define its position, rotation, and scale.

slides.title: Adding & Removing Components ➕
slides.content:
# Customizing Objects

- Click **Add Component** at the bottom of the Inspector to search and attach new components.
- To remove a component, right‑click its header and choose **Remove Component**.
- Some components are dependant (e.g., a Mesh Renderer requires a Mesh Filter). Unity will warn you.

slides.title: Debug Mode & Presets 📋
slides.content:
# Inspector Super Powers

- **Normal vs Debug mode**: Right‑click the Inspector tab → **Debug** to see private variables, backup values, and raw numbers.
- **Component Presets**: Click the gear icon on a component → **Save Current to Preset**. You can later apply that preset to other objects for quick setup.
- **Lock Inspector**: The lock icon at the top makes the Inspector show the same object even if you select something else.

quizData.question: Debug mode in the Inspector shows private fields that are normally hidden.
quizData.explanation: Debug mode reveals all serialized fields, including private ones marked with SerializeField.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Quick Component Search

When adding a component, simply start typing its name. Unity filters the list instantly—no need to scroll.
